title: It needs a folder
story: `split_fasta.py all.fasta OUT_DIR` writes each sequence of all.fasta to its own file in OUT_DIR. Split all.fasta into a folder called {{out}}.

files.~/{{project}}/split_fasta.py:
"""Write each sequence of a FASTA file to its own file in OUT_DIR."""
import sys

fasta, out_dir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
records = []
with open(fasta) as handle:
    for line in handle:
        if line.startswith(">"):
            records.append([line[1:].split()[0], line])
        else:
            records[-1][1] += line

for name, text in records:
    out_path = f"{out_dir}/{name}.fasta"
    with open(out_path, "w") as out:
        out.write(text)
print(f"wrote {len(records)} files to {out_dir}/")

hints: If Python says No such file or directory for a file it is writing, the folder is missing. mkdir {{out}} first.
